intro: Choosing the right area matters more than the hotel itself in Lampang. Here are the main neighborhoods, who each suits, and where to book for your travel style.

blocks.html: Short answer: Lampang is a quiet old town famous for its horse carriages. The Kad Kong Ta area (a Chinese trading street on the Wang River) is the best base — a weekend walking street, handsome old buildings and riverside guesthouses. For convenience choose the town center near the Clock Tower and markets; for nature and quiet resorts head out of town toward Wat Phra That Lampang Luang or Chae Son.

faq.q: Where should I stay in Lampang?
faq.a: The Kad Kong Ta area on the Wang River is best, especially on weekends when the walking street runs — handsome Chinese-European shophouses and riverside guesthouses with a lovely feel. For convenience, choose the town center near the Clock Tower.

faq.q: What is there to do in Lampang?
faq.a: Ride a horse carriage around town, visit Wat Phra That Lampang Luang and Wat Chedi Sao, walk Kad Kong Ta, soak at Chae Son’s hot springs and try the ceramic cafés. Many stop for a day or two on the way to Chiang Mai.

faq.q: Are Lampang and Chiang Mai close?
faq.a: Yes — Lampang is about 100 km from Chiang Mai, roughly 1.5–2 hours by road or train. Many stop in Lampang before or after Chiang Mai because it is quieter and cheaper.
